title: Estimating willingness to pay for urban green improvement and climate change mitigation: a contingent valuation study in Athens, Greece
content:
Abstract
Urban green spaces (UGS) in Athens are highly valued for their environmental and social benefits, yet, as public non-market goods, they lack explicit market prices and tend to be unevenly distributed and underfunded. This study aimed to estimate residents’ willingness to pay (WTP) for an earmarked annual municipal fee to finance a green infrastructure program. A Contingent Valuation survey of 508 adult residents employed a single- and double-bounded dichotomous choice design. Overall, 47.6% of respondents stated a positive WTP, while 52.4% refused any payment. Among refusals, protest zeros predominated at 89.8%, indicating widespread institutional objections rather than indifference. Across valuation models based on single- and double-bounded contingent valuation and a mixture framework accounting for protest responses, bid levels exert a strong negative effect on acceptance, whereas income and pro-urban-greening attitudes are robust positive predictors. Mean annual WTP was estimated at approximately €42–€47 per household. The findings indicate substantial but conditional public support for co-financing UGS improvements, underscoring the importance of credible, transparent, and trusted governance arrangements for the social acceptability of urban greening and climate-resilience policies in Athens.
